Elites are like "Group Captains" for Rank-and-File; so while they aren't physically any larger and don't spawn as frequent as them, they do generally have a higher health pool, different damage multipliers, and spawn more frequently compared to Minibosses and Bosses. Usually they are prefixed with a title like "Resilient" or "Honored" or "Axis" but this isn't always the case.

Elites are (usually) 1 rank above their Rank-and-File variants for the purposes of triggers, energy gains, etc
e.g. a Tier 1 Elite Dreg would provide the same returns for various Modifiers as if it were a Tier 2 Rank-and-File enemy.

What about the "Specialist" Combatants?
Hive Lightbearers, Tormentors, and Subjugators

column9:
Hive Lightbearers manifest and utilise the Light against their foes, including throwing grenades and using Supers that are all too familiar to us Guardians. Upon defeating them you must crush their Ghosts to permanently kill them, otherwise their Ghost will resurrect them back to partial or full health.

There are three Lightbearer Classes each with their own distinct style and abilities:

column9:
Tormentors are big hulking combatants equipped with a scythe. They are initially slow and impervious to damage until both of their shoulders are destroyed where their chest opens up as a weak spot. Damage dealt to anywhere else on a Tormentor's body is harshly reduced.
When their shoulders are destroyed they become enraged and extremely aggressive.

Their heavy scythe attack and jump slam AOE cause Suppression - removing Guardians from their Super and temporarily disabling abilities.

They can grab Guardians with their scythe and siphon energy and health from them - though enough damage dealt by other Guardians will disrupt this grab.

column13:
Subjugators are thin and agile combatants and come equipped with Darkness abilities depending on the type of Subjugator they are.

Omens - the Stasis-wielding Subjugator - can spawn a Resonant Harrier, a Soul-like drone that fires Solar damage, to itself and its allies. Omens fire Stasis projectiles and can spawn a large amount of Stasis Crystals and then 'Heavy' attack to Shatter them all (similar to Winter's Wrath Super). 

Harbingers - the Strand-wielding Subjugator - enhances nearby Dread units. Harbingers fire Strand projectiles and can Suspend their foes, causing them to be weakened and receive increased damage to Harbinger's attacks.

column5:
Both Miniboss- and Boss-tier Subjugators gain 30% DR to all damage after they enrage (usually about 60% health).
Boss-tier Subjugators have a permanent 20% DR to all non-matching damage, meaning Boss Omens are weak to Stasis and Boss Harbingers weak to Strand - effectively counting as their own unique "Shields".

Shield-damaging modifiers are very effective against Boss-tier Subjugators:
Microcosm 300% increased damage, Under-Over 50-55% increased damage, and Adaptive Munitions 40-80% (depending on weapon archetype) increased damage.

column8:
If Specialist Units have a "Minibosses" icon they are classified as a Miniboss

Miniboss Lightbearers/Tormentors are susceptible to:
• Being Slowed and Frozen by Stasis
• Suppressed/Blinded/Disoriented (unable to fire)
• Be Suspended
• They can be Finished like other Minibosses
(note: Lightbearers generally cannot be Finished, but Finishing their Ghosts does count as a "Finisher")

They are affected by any modifier that affects Minibosses.
column24:
If the Specialist Units have a "Bosses" icon they are classified as a Boss

• Boss variants are immune to the effects of Slow and Freeze by Stasis
(but Stasis can still be "applied" to activate effects like Focusing Lens)
• They can be Suppressed (e.g. knocked out of their Supers) but will still be able to fire
(note: this does not apply to Raid/Dungeon/end-game activity Bosses)
• They cannot be physically Suspended but the effect is still applied on them
• Boss Tormentors and Subjugators cannot be Finished

They are affected by any any modifier that affects Bosses.

column7:
What about Lost Sector Bosses?
"I keep hearing these are all Minibosses so I shouldn't test on them!?"

Okay - so this is partially true. Lost Sector "Bosses" are EITHER Minibosses OR Bosses - depending on the location of the Lost Sector.
Should you do testing on them? Honestly there are much better (and faster) areas to do damage/DPS testing. Places like Kalli or Gambit Private Matches are perfectly fine to test things (those are where I test things), but if you REALLY want to use a Lost Sector "Boss" you need to test on those that are actually Bosses; using the Nessus Colossus is absolutely terrible for testing because he is a Miniboss (has different multipliers and modifiers applied to him) and gives off a false narrative of what is and isn't actually good. Please stop using him for most testing purposes.

Banes are Combatant-affixed modifiers that grant unique abilities to enemies. They can be any non-Boss type of combatant.

Depending on the type they either have 35% or 60% damage resistance to all damage.

They can be found in high-level activities, destinations, and the "Feat: Battalions" modifier.

column13:
Minibosses can be described as "Sector Chiefs" - they are much larger in appearance than both Rank-and-File and Elites but do no spawn as regular.
They can be much bulkier targets and can pack a punch for those unprepared, but do not possess any abilities that Champions have.

Most, but not all, of the time they also come equipped with an Elemental Shield.
MADE BY @COURTPROJECTS

Champions are, for all intents and purposes, just Minibosses with extra steps:
Barrier -- Colossus, Servitor, Knight, and Hobgoblin
Overload -- Captain, Chieftain, Taken Hobgoblin, and Minotaur
Unstoppable -- Incendior, Ogre, Abomination, and Taken Phalanx

For more information regarding Champions including types, weapon counters, Artifact Mods, and how to effectively deal with them
see this Champions Tab here

From Strikes to Raids to even some that roam in Patrol spaces, these are top of the food chain. Bosses can be imposing threats, being visually larger and defensively tankier than Minibosses. Some Bosses can have their own immunity phases, some Bosses have their own unique damage capabilities, and some Bosses even look a lot different than "it's a Captain but larger".

So, are Bosses split into sub-families? From a general perspective the answer is actually no. Sure, some Bosses like Kalli and Shiro Chi have double precision multipliers but that doesn't make them a seperate "Boss" and they have no other differences to Templar or Taniks outside of damage scaling due to Light Levels or the type of activity.

The primary sub-family of Constructs - these are objects that possess the ability to move around and have a physical appearance and presence of a tank, ship, or one-seater vehicle. Taken Blights also count as a "Vehicle" however little sense that makes.

column5:
Despite their appearances to suggest otherwise, there are a few Combatants
that are NOT classified as any Construct whatsoever:

• Servitors, and Shanks (including Heavy and Sniper variants)
• Vex Hydras and Wyverns (Gorgons are Elites)

Their Classification would be whatever icon they have.
So a Heavy Shank with a Square Icon means they are (High-Tier) Rank-and-File.
column23:
Boss Combatants like Sepiks Prime, SABER, The Warden - as well as any potential outliers like Lost Sector Servitors, Savathûn, etc - also are not considered "Constructs". They are Bosses, and have "Boss" multipliers.

The only outlier worthwhile to highlight are Oryx's Daughters - they erroneously had "Elite" multipliers attached to them despite having a Boss Icon. This was fixed a while ago and is no longer the case.

Dul Incaru is still erroneously assigned as an "Elite" Combatant.
